correctness.rationale: All affine-plane axioms and both line-parallel / line-intersecting distance cases are used explicitly. The point-localization bound yields the exact minimum and unique parallel-class equality. A distinct exhaustive near-minimum case division establishes the q+1 gap for q>=3 and six exceptions at q=2. The exchange threshold follows from pairwise disjoint bases. Python exhaustive BFS interval census confirms q=2,3,4; C++17 independent Floyd--Warshall confirms q=2,3. No finite checks are used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The closest public result classifies projective-plane incidence geodetic bases and a different exchange law. Its theorem applies to a distinct graph with different distances, and does not imply the affine-plane interval or minimal-gap classification. The archival primary sources examine general graph-geodetic parameters, not affine-plane line-class coverage. Specific resolvable-design and affine-plane geodetic searches revealed no direct or stronger record. Residual risks from unindexed literature are retained.
residual_risks: The publisher full text of Chartrand–Harary–Zhang (2000) was inaccessible at the notice link; it was not certified absent from that full text.
Unindexed older geodetic studies of affine or resolvable designs might contain an equivalent invariant or table; no absolute priority is asserted.
Only q=2,3,4 were computationally exhausted; the general conclusion depends on the printed incidence proof.

value.rationale: A natural complete all-order classification for a classical family of finite incidence graphs, not a renamed textbook calculation: geodetic bases consist exclusively of the q+1 parallel classes, simultaneous relocation has a sharp all-at-once threshold q, and there is a missing q+1 cardinality in the inclusion-minimal spectrum for all q>=3, with exactly six exceptional minimal sets at q=2. These compare meaningfully with the different projective-plane flag-basis theorem. No large theorem or downstream application is asserted beyond the intrinsic classification.
